purpose: Determine whether the sources already bound to R5.17 provide a direct, governed persistent freshwater availability/reliability field suitable for civilization-facing human support.
scope_rule: This audit evaluates currently bound and explicitly identified SEALED authorities. It does not claim that no freshwater-relevant quantity exists anywhere in historical archives.

evidence_summary.r5_17_a: Hydrology/water reliability is PARTIAL; freshwater_support, freshwater_reliability, persistent_water_access and navigable_water_opportunity are explicitly missing and require new compute.
evidence_summary.r5_17_b1_b3: The bound R3.18/R3.19/R3.20 inputs supply environmental exposure integrals, a 0-ka accessibility endpoint and a 15-11 ka hazard layer; none is authorized as direct human freshwater supply.
evidence_summary.r3_20: Hydrological outputs are diagnostic/ranking hazard variables, not flood depths, guaranteed inundation, freshwater availability or a generic human-support penalty.
evidence_summary.r3_14: The late-Cenozoic binding points to exact historical v0.6.1 paleoclimate payloads whose raw array inventory has not yet been promoted into R5.17 freshwater semantics.

next_question: Do the exact R3.14-bound v0.6.1 paleoclimate payloads contain precipitation, moisture, runoff, drainage, storage, lake, river or other physically interpretable fields that can support a native freshwater derivation?
